headline: Vocab Sprint: Build Precise Vocabulary in Context
problemStatement: Learners often understand a word on a quiz but still reach for a vague choice when they speak or write. VocabSprint gives them a short sentence with one weak word and asks them to replace it with a stronger alternative that fits the context. The class can then discuss what makes a word precise.
outcomes: Replace vague words with alternatives that communicate a clearer idea.
Compare register and meaning so an upgrade fits the sentence, not just a thesaurus list.
Build vocabulary retrieval speed through repeated, short choices.
howItWorks: Choose a topic and difficulty. The game creates short sentences and marks one intentionally weak word for students to improve.
During a race, each learner submits an upgrade on a phone. A turn-based option lets the teacher work with one student at a time.
The game evaluates whether a suggestion fits the meaning, context, and register; it is not limited to a single exact-match answer.
At review, the best upgrade is swapped into the sentence. The answer wall keeps names private apart from the winner, and useful words can be collected in a word bank for later rounds.
teacherUseCases: Warm up a writing lesson with stronger verbs or adjectives drawn from the current unit topic.
Use the step-through review to compare a suggested word with the original sentence, then ask students to explain why it fits.

faq.q: Does VocabSprint accept more than one correct upgrade?
faq.a: Yes. Suggestions are judged for context and quality rather than exact matching alone, so different words can work when they keep the sentence accurate and stronger.
The game evaluates each answer and shows a class review. A strong upgrade replaces the weak word in the sentence, giving everyone context for discussion.

faq.q: Can I use my own topic?
faq.a: Choose the lesson topic or enter a custom one when available. Generated sentences give students a fresh setting for applying unit vocabulary.

faq.q: How does the word bank help?
faq.a: The bank collects strong upgrades and suggested words across rounds. Teachers can return to it during a later writing task or use it as a class vocabulary recap.
